subject: Banking
title: Tokenization of Real Assets
description: A fast breakdown of Tokenization of Real Assets for builders.

hook.text: JPMorgan tokenized $1 billion in Treasury bonds on a blockchain. Real-world assets are moving on-chain.

buildup.text: Tokenization means representing ownership of real assets like property, bonds, or art as digital tokens on a blockchain.

discovery.text: Fractional ownership becomes easy. You could own 0.001% of a Manhattan building through a $100 token purchase.

twist.text: A token can move instantly on-chain while the legal claim still depends on courts and paperwork.

climax.text: The real breakthrough is faster settlement for assets that used to trade slowly and expensively.

punchline.text: Own 0.001% of a building for $100. The tech works. The law does not.

quiz.question: What is the main challenge with tokenizing real-world assets?
options: Legal frameworks haven't caught up to handle ownership and liability issues

details.summary: Tokenization converts ownership of real-world assets like real estate, art, and bonds into digital tokens on a blockchain, enabling fractional ownership, 24/7 trading, and instant settlement of traditionally illiquid assets.
details.whyItMatters: Tokenization could unlock trillions in currently illiquid assets by making fractional ownership and instant trading possible. Owning a fraction of a commercial building or fine art collection becomes as easy as buying a stock.
takeaways: Real estate, bonds, art, and commodities can be tokenized for fractional ownership
BlackRock and JPMorgan are actively building tokenization platforms
Smart contracts automate dividend payments, transfers, and compliance

faq.question: What is the advantage of tokenized real estate?
faq.answer: You could own a fraction of a commercial building for as little as one hundred dollars, receive proportional rental income automatically, and sell your token on a marketplace anytime. Traditional real estate requires hundreds of thousands and takes months to sell.

faq.question: Is tokenization regulated?
faq.answer: Regulatory frameworks are developing. Tokenized securities generally fall under existing securities laws, but the technology creates new questions about custody, settlement, and investor protection that regulators are still addressing.
